item.description: Cork remain on top of Division One A of the National Hurling League. Barry Walsh, Alan Walsh and Brian Hayes scored the goals as the Rebels beat Kilkenny by 3-12 to 1-15 to make it make four wins from four. Galway have picked up a crucial win in their bid to beat the drop. Advertisement Colm Molloy and Ronan Glennon hit the net as the Tribesmen overcame Waterford by 2-18 to 16-points in Salthill. item.title: Premier League review
item.description: Manchester United have gone third in the Premier League with a 2-1 comeback win over 10-man Crystal Palace. The game turned in the second-half when United got a penalty. Tottenham lost again and were beaten 2-1 at Fulham. Advertisement But fellow strugglers Nottingham Forest couldn't capitalise and suffered defeat by the same score at Brighton.

item.title: Harry Byrne out of match against Wales
item.description: Harry Byrne has been ruled out of Ireland's Six Nations match against Wales next week. The Leinster out-half suffered a concussion this weekend, while Ulster forward Cormac Izuchukwu will link up with the squad as he continues to go through the return to play protocols. item.title: Councillor criticises TII for the appalling condition of national secondary roads in Kerry
item.description: The state on the national secondary roads in Kerry, particularly the N70 is beyond appalling. That’s according to Fine Gael councillor Tommy Griffin, who tabled a motion for funding to address the routes surface. Speaking at the recent Castleisland-Corca Dhuibhne MD meeting, he slammed Transport Infrastructure Ireland, describing them as "invisible". item.title: People aged 55 or over urged to complete survey relating to new Age Friendly Strategy for Kerry
item.description: People aged 55 or over are being urged to complete a survey relating to the development of a new Age Friendly Strategy for Kerry. This strategy aims to make Kerry a place where people can live well and age positively. This survey has been launched in addition to the public consultation sessions that are currently underway across the county. item.title: Ireland open qualification campaign with win
item.description: Ireland have opened their qualification campaign for the men's hockey World Cup with a win. Mark Tumilty's side have beaten Canada 5-2 in Chile. Ireland's next match will see them take on Korea on Tuesday. Advertisement
